proofs.proof_tex:
Fix rational \(\eta\) and rational \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\cup
\mathcal M_{\eta,1}^{1\mathrm c}\).  We first prove the general algorithmic
claim and then verify the directed benchmark execution.

Because \(P=F(\psi)\) for some \(\psi\in\Theta_\eta\), the arm probabilities
satisfy
\[
p_1=\sum_{z=1}^2\pi_z e_z\geq
\eta\sum_{z=1}^2\pi_z=\eta,
\qquad
p_0=\sum_{z=1}^2\pi_z(1-e_z)\geq
\eta\sum_{z=1}^2\pi_z=\eta.
\]
Thus all conditional probabilities in \(H_d\) and \(N_d\) are defined.  Since
the cells of \(P\) and \(\eta\) are rational, every coefficient in every
cleared branch system is rational.  Multiplication by the product of its
positive integer denominators converts it into a finite family of integer
polynomials without changing any equality or sign.

The algorithm in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}one\text{-}collision\text{-}algorithm}\)
enumerates
\[
2\cdot 2^3\cdot 2=32
\]
labels \((k_0,s,\sigma)\).  For each fixed label, Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}observable\text{-}sign\text{-}certificate}\) applies the full
projection operator to every unordered pair of current polynomials, including
equality--equality pairs.  Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}cad\text{-}quantifier\text{-}elimination}\) therefore gives a
finite sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition and a terminating
signed lifting computation for that branch.  A finite loop of thirty-two
terminating computations terminates.

There is a unique \(k_\ast\in\mathcal A\) such that
\(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_\ast}^{1\mathrm c}\).  Indeed, membership for both
values would require every member of the nonempty global fiber to have a
collision at \(k=0\) and a noncollision at \(k=1\), and simultaneously a
collision at \(k=1\) and a noncollision at \(k=0\), a contradiction.  For
\(k_0=k_\ast\), Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}dimension\text{-}reduction}\) says that reconstruction maps
the union of the sixteen feasible ten-variable chart solution sets onto the
entire labeled fiber.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}quotient\text{-}att}\) then shows
that quotienting simultaneous type labels changes neither reconstructed ATT
coordinate.  Consequently the disjunction of the accepted chart images is
exactly \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).

For \(k_0\neq k_\ast\), suppose a chart were accepted.  Its positive masses
and eight equations \(\rho_{zdj}=0\) factor its prefix array into two
arm-local Markov components; its four equations
\(\gamma_{zi}^{\sigma}=0\) impose a common pre-treatment transition after the
relative alignment \(\sigma\); and its terminal split and positive-mass
ratios reconstruct all primitives in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).  The identities in
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}ten\text{-}variable\text{-}system}\) then give a
\(\psi\in\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).  This contradicts
\(\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\subseteq\Theta_{\eta,k_\ast}^{1\mathrm c}\).
Therefore every wrong-state chart is rejected and both its branch union and
\(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) are empty.  The returned joint image is
hence exact for each \(k_0\), rather than an outer approximation.

To obtain the displayed output grammar, introduce retained coordinates
\((q_3,q_4)\), adjoin
\[
q_t=\tau_t\!\left(
\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P\right),
\qquad t\in\{3,4\},
\]
and clear only the positive denominators recorded by the branch system.
Quantifier elimination gives an equivalent Boolean combination of
integer-polynomial sign conditions in \((q_3,q_4)\).  Taking the disjunction
over the accepted labels gives the asserted exact joint formula.

It remains to justify attainment and the marginal grammar.  The set
\(\Theta_\eta\) is a closed and bounded subset of a finite-dimensional
Euclidean space, hence compact.  The map \(F\) is polynomial and therefore
continuous, so
\[
K(P)=\{\psi\in\Theta_\eta:F(\psi)=P\}
\]
is compact.  For the unique \(k_\ast\), exclusivity gives
\(K(P)=\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_\ast}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).
The only division in \(w_{z1}\) is by \(p_1\geq\eta>0\), and the untreated
recurrences are polynomial in the primitive probabilities.  Hence
\(\psi\mapsto\tau(\psi;P)\) is continuous on \(K(P)\).  Its joint image and
both coordinate images are compact, and every coordinate boundary is
attained.

Each marginal is semialgebraic by the preceding elimination.  The finitely
many nonzero univariate polynomials in its quantifier-free formula have
finitely many real roots.  Those roots partition the line into finitely many
points and open intervals on which all atomic signs are constant.  Compactness
therefore makes each selected marginal a finite ordered union of closed
intervals and isolated points.  With rational input, every boundary root is
real algebraic.  Square-free factorization, rational root isolation, and
derivative-sign evaluation provide its square-free integer polynomial,
rational isolating interval, and Thom signs.  At an endpoint, compactness
supplies an attaining point of \(K(P)\); dimension reduction places it in an
accepted labeled chart, and CAD lifting gives a real-algebraic \(y\), so the
reconstruction formulas give a feasible real-algebraic structural witness.
For a discarded branch, complete sign-invariant lifting partitions every
candidate into finitely many lifting cells; recording on every candidate cell
the first violated original atom is an exact infeasibility certificate.
Nothing in this argument shortens Collins projection or its generic schedule,
so no generic worst-case complexity improvement is claimed.

We now verify the fixed execution record at \(\eta=1/10\),
\(\vartheta=0\), and \(P=P^\diamond\).  Direct substitution in \(F\) gives the
following thirty-two reduced cells; each key is \(ijkld\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|c@{\quad}c|c@{\quad}c|c@{\quad}c|c}
00000&259/5000&00001&469/6250&00010&259/5000&00011&889/25000\\
00100&357/12500&00101&1743/50000&00110&721/25000&00111&1827/50000\\
01000&357/20000&01001&21/1250&01010&357/20000&01011&93/5000\\
01100&621/50000&01101&147/10000&01110&261/12500&01111&279/10000\\
10000&33/2500&10001&48/3125&10010&33/2500&10011&69/6250\\
10100&99/6250&10101&153/12500&10110&147/12500&10111&117/12500\\
11000&171/2500&11001&24/625&11010&171/2500&11011&42/625\\
11100&243/6250&11101&21/625&11110&126/3125&11111&33/625
\end{array}
\]
Exact addition gives
\[
\sum_{i,j,k,l,d}P^\diamond_{ijkld}=1,
\qquad
\sum_{i,j,k,l}P^\diamond_{ijkl0}
=\sum_{i,j,k,l}P^\diamond_{ijkl1}=\frac12.
\]
The two benchmark representations have the same treated components and
treated weights.  Their control components and control weights are
simultaneously exchanged, so term-by-term evaluation of the two-component
mixture gives
\[
F(\psi^\diamond)_{ijkld}
=F(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}})_{ijkld}
=P^\diamond_{ijkld}
\]
for every one of the thirty-two keys.

From these cells, exact conditioning produces \(H\) and \(N\).  The three
required control minors at \(k_0=0\) are
\[
\chi_{00}^{01}=\chi_{00}^{10}=\chi_{00}^{11}=0,
\]
whereas a concrete required minor for \(k_0=1\) is
\[
\chi_{01}^{01}
=N_0(0,1,1)H_0(0,0,1)-N_0(0,0,1)H_0(0,1,1)
=\frac{11907}{12500000}>0.
\]
Thus every one of the sixteen \(k_0=1\) labels is rejected by the same
explicit nonzero equality atom.

For \(k_0=0\), exact recovery before orientation lifting is finite.  To see
this without treating the benchmark proposition as an execution oracle, let
\(Q^d_{jk}\) be the \(2\)-by-\(2\) matrix with row \(l\), column \(i\), and
entry
\[
Q^d_{jk}(l,i)
=P^\diamond(X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=k,X_4=l\mid D=d).
\]
For any two-type arm decomposition, the path factorization gives
\[
Q^d_{jk}
=V_k\operatorname{diag}\!\bigl(
B(q_{1j};k),B(q_{2j};k)\bigr)S_j,
\]
where column \(z\) of \(V_k\) is
\((1-v_{zk},v_{zk})^{\mathsf T}\) and
\(S_j(z,i)=w_{zd}B(u_{zd};i)B(a_{zi};j)\).  On the treated arm the two
terminal determinants are \(3/5\) and \(2/5\), while
\[
\det S_0=\frac{21}{3125},
\qquad
\det S_1=\frac{36}{3125}.
\]
Thus all four \(Q^1_{jk}\) are invertible.  Cancellation of these
factorizations gives
\[
Q^1_{01}(Q^1_{00})^{-1}Q^1_{10}(Q^1_{11})^{-1}
=V_1\operatorname{diag}(9/49,6)V_1^{-1}.
\]
The eigenvalue gap is \(285/49\neq0\), so the two normalized eigenspaces
recover \(V_1\) up to permutation.  Column normalization in
\[
Q^1_{00}(Q^1_{01})^{-1}V_1
=V_0\operatorname{diag}\!\left(
\frac{1-q_{10}}{q_{10}},\frac{1-q_{20}}{q_{20}}\right)
\]
recovers \(V_0\) in the same order, and
\[
S_j=V_0^{-1}Q^1_{j0}+V_1^{-1}Q^1_{j1}
\]
then recovers the remaining treated-arm primitives by positive row and
column sums.  Hence the treated decomposition has exactly two labeled
orders, and in either order it recovers
\[
a_{10}=a_{20}=\frac3{10},
\qquad
a_{11}=a_{21}=\frac45.
\]

For the control arm define
\[
g_{ij}=P^\diamond(X_3=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,D=0),
\quad
h_{ij}=P^\diamond(X_3=1,X_4=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,D=0).
\]
The recovered equality of the two \(a\)-rows makes the latent type
conditionally independent of \(X_2\) given \(X_1,D=0\).  With
\(\lambda_i=P(Z=1\mid X_1=i,D=0)\), this gives
\[
g_{ij}=\lambda_iq_{1j}+(1-\lambda_i)q_{2j}.
\]
The observable row differences are
\[
g_{00}-g_{10}=-\frac{32}{207},
\qquad
g_{01}-g_{11}=\frac8{69}.
\]
They imply both \(\lambda_0\neq\lambda_1\) and
\(q_{1j}\neq q_{2j}\).  The observed equality
\[
P^\diamond(X_4=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=0,D=0)=\frac12
\]
gives two linear equations in \(v_{10}-1/2\) and \(v_{20}-1/2\).
Their determinants are \(128/1035\) and \(112/1035\), so
\[
v_{10}=v_{20}=\frac12.
\]
For the remaining terminal row, exact slopes and intercepts of \(h\) as an
affine function of \(g\) give
\[
q_{z0}(v_{z1}-1/4)=\frac9{100},
\qquad
q_{z1}(v_{z1}-1)=-\frac9{50}.
\]
The two distinct values of \(\lambda_i\), applied to the observed identities
\(g_{i1}=3(1-g_{i0})/4\), also give
\[
q_{z1}=\frac34(1-q_{z0}).
\]
Eliminating \(q_{z0}\) from these three equalities yields
\[
(5v-2)(10v-7)=0.
\]
It has exactly the roots \(2/5\) and \(7/10\).  The nonzero row differences
forbid assigning the same root to both components, so the control
decomposition has exactly two labeled orders.  Their Cartesian product is
exactly
\[
\begin{aligned}
y_{AA}&=(1/5,4/5,7/10,3/10,7/10,2/5,
98/625,21/625,12/625,24/625),\\
y_{AB}&=(1/5,4/5,7/10,3/10,2/5,7/10,
63/1250,189/5000,21/625,147/625),\\
y_{BA}&=(4/5,1/5,3/10,7/10,7/10,2/5,
98/625,21/625,12/625,24/625),\\
y_{BB}&=(4/5,1/5,3/10,7/10,2/5,7/10,
63/1250,189/5000,21/625,147/625).
\end{aligned}
\]
Direct substitution gives all eight \(\rho\)-values and all four
\(\gamma^\sigma\)-values equal to zero for each allowed alignment.  The
smallest strict orientation value is \(3/10\), the smallest value of
\(R_{zd}(i,j,k)-\eta^5\) is \(479/100000\), and the smallest primitive box
slack is \(1/10\).  Thus no equality, positivity, or box atom has been omitted.

In the sign order
\((s_{0,1-k_0},s_{1,0},s_{1,1})\), these four leaves have signs
\[
(+,-,+),\quad(-,-,+),\quad(+,+,-),\quad(-,+,-),
\]
respectively.  Both relative alignments are feasible at every leaf, giving
exactly eight accepted labels.  Reconstruction gives, in the same leaf order,
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{leaf}&\sigma=\mathrm{id}&\sigma=\mathrm{sw}\\ \hline
y_{AA}&\psi^\diamond&\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\\
y_{AB}&\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}&\psi^\diamond\\
y_{BA}&\mathrm{sw}\,\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}&
       \mathrm{sw}\,\psi^\diamond\\
y_{BB}&\mathrm{sw}\,\psi^\diamond&
       \mathrm{sw}\,\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}} .
\end{array}
\]
For each of the four sign triples whose two treated signs agree, the four
displayed points exhaust the equality-lifting leaves and each violates a
strict orientation atom.  Recording the first such violation at every leaf
rejects all eight remaining \(k_0=0\) labels.  Together with the sixteen
wrong-collision rejections, this accounts for all twenty-four discarded
labels.

Evaluating the ATT recurrences at the accepted reconstructions gives only
\[
\tau(\psi^\diamond;P^\diamond)
=\left(\frac9{250},-\frac{33}{2500}\right),
\qquad
\tau(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}};P^\diamond)
=\left(-\frac1{500},\frac{49}{5000}\right);
\]
simultaneous swaps give the same values by Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}quotient\text{-}att}\).  Hence the normalized joint output is
\[
\bigl(250q_3-9=0\ \wedge\ 2500q_4+33=0\bigr)
\ \vee\
\bigl(500q_3+1=0\ \wedge\ 5000q_4-49=0\bigr),
\]
with marginals
\[
(500q_3+1=0)\vee(250q_3-9=0),
\qquad
(2500q_4+33=0)\vee(5000q_4-49=0).
\]
The four isolating intervals are, in the corresponding marginal order,
\[
\left(-\frac1{400},-\frac1{600}\right),\quad
\left(\frac1{30},\frac1{25}\right),\quad
\left(-\frac7{500},-\frac{13}{1000}\right),\quad
\left(\frac9{1000},\frac1{100}\right).
\]
Each defining polynomial is primitive linear with positive derivative, so
under the convention
\((\operatorname{sgn}p(\alpha),\operatorname{sgn}p'(\alpha),\ldots)\)
every Thom sequence is \((0,+)\).

The machine-readable record
\(\texttt{art:p-diamond-onecollisionatt-v1}\) stores every rational value just
used, all \(H,N,\chi\) values, all accepted-branch original-atom evaluations,
the eight full reconstructed representations with thirty-two zero cellwise
differences, and the complete four-leaf rejection audit for every same-sign
treated branch.  Its deterministic replay recomputes these quantities with
reduced integer fractions and compares the complete canonical serialization
byte for byte.  This is one fixed-input instantiation of the proved algorithm,
not a compressed diagnostic or a stronger theorem.

proposed.construction:
For every \(\vartheta\in(-1/100,1/100)\), let
\(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\) be obtained from \(\psi^{\diamond}\) by
replacing only \(c_{130}=3/10\) by
\(c_{130}(\vartheta)=3/10+\vartheta\), and let
\(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\) be obtained from
\(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\) by the identical replacement of its treated
coordinate.  All other primitive coordinates are unchanged.  Define
\(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}=F(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})\).  Thus
\(\psi^{\diamond}_{0}=\psi^{\diamond}\),
\(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{0}=\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\), and

proposed.name: Exact one-collision ATT algorithm
proposed.construction:
\(\mathsf{OneCollisionATT}(P,\eta)\) takes reduced rational encodings of
\(\eta\) and the thirty-two cells of \(P\); enumerates exactly
\(2\cdot2^3\cdot2=32\) labeled branches \((k_0,s,\sigma)\); builds each
ten-variable system \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}\); performs the fixed Collins
projection and signed Sturm--Habicht lifting in
\(\mathrm{def{:}observable\text{-}sign\text{-}certificate}\); and projects
each retained cell through
\(\tau(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P)\).  The joint image is
returned as a quantifier-free Boolean combination of integer-polynomial sign
conditions in \((\tau_3,\tau_4)\).  Each marginal is returned as an ordered
finite union of closed intervals and isolated points whose endpoints have a
square-free integer polynomial, rational isolating interval, and Thom sign
sequence.  Every endpoint carries a reconstructed real-algebraic \(\psi\) and
its \((k_0,s,\sigma)\) label; every discarded branch carries an exact sign or
polynomial infeasibility certificate.  For the fixed specialization
\(\eta=1/10\), \(\vartheta=0\), and \(P=P^\diamond\), its canonical
machine-readable execution is the object
\(\texttt{art:p-diamond-onecollisionatt-v1}\) in
\(\texttt{discovery/p\_diamond\_onecollisionatt.json}\).  The deterministic
checker
\(\texttt{discovery/replay\_p\_diamond\_onecollisionatt.mjs}\) reconstructs
\(P,H,N,\chi,\mathscr G\), all thirty-two branch dispositions, the two ATT
values, and the Thom encodings using reduced exact rational arithmetic, then
requires byte-for-byte equality with that literal payload.

prose_updates.tldr: On the compact binary four-period model, the completed singular result is the exclusive stratum with distinct treated terminal rows and exactly one collided control terminal row. Terminal splitting reduces its forty-coordinate labeled fiber to sixteen ten-variable orientation and alignment charts for each collided state. A corrected full Collins certificate projects every pair in the complete polynomial family and exactly decides branch feasibility and aggregate-ATT constancy, including zero and box-face cells; it is a generic exact certificate, not the still-open compressed economic sign basis. The exact algorithm returns the attained, possibly disconnected sharp image with endpoint witnesses. A deterministic exact-rational execution artifact now instantiates all thirty-two branches at the prescribed benchmark, including literal full-path cells, accepted reconstructions, complete rejected-leaf audits, and Thom encodings. Full-PMF inversion remains auxiliary; no endpoint or Hausdorff consistency is claimed. An injective one-parameter family has two separated quotient ATT values, proving positive-dimensional persistence but not relative openness in a larger collision variety.

project_justification.fill: The project proves the corrected arm-label-aware ten-coordinate reconstruction, uses a complete all-pairs Collins projection certificate to classify feasibility and point identification on that stratum, computes its exact attained ATT image, and supplies auxiliary finite-sample full-PMF coverage. The prescribed benchmark is now accompanied by a deterministic exact-rational execution record covering all thirty-two branch labels, without presenting that record as a compressed diagnostic or a general implementation. A separate injective one-parameter family proves persistent two-value ambiguity. Compression of the complete certificate to a smaller irredundant observable basis remains open.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The empirical thirty-two-cell path PMF is inverted over all thirty-two labeled one-collision branches; no relative alignment is selected before projection. The fixed benchmark artifact is an exact-rational regression and audit fixture, not an additional sampling assumption.

prose_updates.interpretation: A reported ATT sign on this merger stratum is identified only when the complete two-copy certificate rejects every feasible unequal-ATT pair across all orientations and both relative alignments. Otherwise the estimand is the attained set itself, which may be disconnected and must not be replaced by its convex hull. The fixed benchmark artifact demonstrates the backend audit grammar with literal cells, reconstructions, branch dispositions, and endpoint encodings. It is not a short economically interpretable front-end diagnostic; certificate compression remains open.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The completed algebra covers only laws whose entire compact fiber has distinct treated terminal rows and exactly one specified collided control terminal row. The certificate uses complete all-pairs Collins quantifier elimination and may have its generic worst-case cost. The new machine-readable record is one fixed exact-rational execution, not evidence for implementation-wide complexity, a compressed sign basis, endpoint or Hausdorff consistency, near-collision behavior, or a global collision atlas. The positive-dimensional benchmark is one explicit affine family and is not claimed relatively open in the full collision variety.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Completed claims are quotient invariance, the corrected forty-to-ten one-collision reduction, the complete thirty-two-branch feasibility and ATT-constancy certificate across both collided states, the exact attained stratum-restricted region, the explicit positive-dimensional two-value family, and uniformly honest finite-sample full-PMF inversion. The added benchmark payload is a replayable fixed-input instantiation of the existing exact algorithm: it adds no theorem, tier claim, compressed diagnostic, global atlas, near-collision theory, or endpoint and Hausdorff asymptotics. No overlap, inclusion, or extension relation with the regular Ahn--Kasahara identification class is claimed.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,3/20)\) and \(\vartheta\in\mathbb R\) with \(|\vartheta|<1/100\).  We first verify support and equality of the two observed laws.  The only perturbed primitive obeys
\[
 \frac{29}{100}<\frac{3}{10}+\vartheta<\frac{31}{100}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Every other primitive in either displayed representation lies in \([1/5,4/5]\).  Since \(\eta<3/20<1/5\) and \(U=1-\eta>17/20>4/5\), (1) and the displayed benchmark coordinates imply
\[
 \psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta},\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\in\Theta_\eta,
 \tag{2}
\]
with strict slack at every face of the probability box.

For \(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\), direct use of the definitions of \(p_d\) and \(w_{zd}\) gives
\[
 p_1=\frac12\frac35+\frac12\frac25=\frac12,
 \qquad p_0=\frac12,
 \qquad (w_{10},w_{20})=\left(\frac25,\frac35\right),
 \qquad (w_{11},w_{21})=\left(\frac35,\frac25\right).
 \tag{3}
\]
For \(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\), the type probabilities are \((3/5,2/5)\) and both assignment probabilities equal \(1/2\), so its posterior weights are \((3/5,2/5)\) in both arms.  Its treated components and their treated weights are those of \(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\).  In the control arm it assigns weight \(3/5\) to the former second component and weight \(2/5\) to the former first component.  Commutativity of the two summands in the definition of \(F\), applied separately to each arm and each full-path cell, therefore yields
\[
 F(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})_{ijkld}
 =F(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta})_{ijkld}
 =P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta,ijkld}
 \quad(i,j,k,l,d\in\mathcal A).
 \tag{4}
\]

We next prove that (4) exhausts the global fiber.  For a fixed arm \(d\), define the observable \(2\)-by-\(2\) matrices, with row index \(l\) and column index \(i\), by
\[
 Q_{jk}^{d}(l,i)=P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=k,X_4=l\mid D=d).
\]
In any two-type representation of this conditional law, put \(q_{zj}=\kappa_{zd3j}\), \(v_{zk}=\kappa_{zd4k}\), let the \(z\)-th column of \(V_k\) be \((1-v_{zk},v_{zk})^{\mathsf T}\), and set
\[
 S_j(z,i)=w_{zd}B(u_{zd};i)B(a_{zi};j).
\]
The full-path factorization gives, entry by entry,
\[
 Q_{jk}^{d}=V_k\operatorname{diag}\!\left(B(q_{1j};k),B(q_{2j};k)\right)S_j.
 \tag{5}
\]

In the treated arm of the displayed representation,
\[
 |\det V_0|=\frac35,
 \qquad |\det V_1|=\frac25.
 \tag{6}
\]
Because \(a_{10}=a_{20}=3/10\) and \(a_{11}=a_{21}=4/5\), direct expansion of \(\det S_j\) gives
\[
 \det S_j=w_{11}w_{21}B(3/10;j)B(4/5;j)(u_{21}-u_{11}),
\]
and hence
\[
 \det S_0=\frac{21}{3125},
 \qquad \det S_1=\frac{36}{3125}.
 \tag{7}
\]
Every factor \(B(q_{zj};k)\) in (5) is at least \(1/5\) for \(|\vartheta|<1/100\).  Thus (5)--(7) imply the uniform observable recovery-minor bound
\[
 |\det Q_{jk}^{1}|\ge
 \frac25\left(\frac15\right)^2\frac{21}{3125}
 =\frac{42}{390625}>0.
 \tag{8}
\]
All four treated matrices are therefore invertible.  Cancellation in (5) gives
\[
 Q_{01}^{1}(Q_{00}^{1})^{-1}Q_{10}^{1}(Q_{11}^{1})^{-1}
 =V_1\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1(\vartheta),\lambda_2)V_1^{-1},
 \tag{9}
\]
where
\[
 \lambda_1(\vartheta)
 =\frac{\operatorname{odds}(3/10+\vartheta)}{\operatorname{odds}(7/10)}
 =\frac{3(3+10\vartheta)}{7(7-10\vartheta)},
 \qquad
 \lambda_2
 =\frac{\operatorname{odds}(3/5)}{\operatorname{odds}(1/5)}=6.
 \tag{10}
\]
Monotonicity of the first rational function and \(|\vartheta|<1/100\) give
\[
 0<\lambda_1(\vartheta)<\frac{31}{161},
 \qquad
 (\lambda_2-\lambda_1(\vartheta))^2>\left(\frac{935}{161}\right)^2>0.
 \tag{11}
\]
The two one-dimensional eigenspaces of the observable matrix in (9) are consequently exactly the two columns of \(V_1\).  Normalizing each column to sum to one recovers \(V_1\) up to permutation.  Moreover,
\[
 Q_{00}^{1}(Q_{01}^{1})^{-1}V_1
 =V_0\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{1-q_{10}}{q_{10}},\frac{1-q_{20}}{q_{20}}\right),
 \tag{12}
\]
so column normalization recovers \(V_0\) in the same order.  Finally,
\[
 S_j=V_0^{-1}Q_{j0}^{1}+V_1^{-1}Q_{j1}^{1}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Indeed, the summands on the right equal \(\operatorname{diag}(1-q_{1j},1-q_{2j})S_j\) and \(\operatorname{diag}(q_{1j},q_{2j})S_j\).  Their row sums recover \(q_{zj}\); summing \(S_0+S_1\), whose entries and row sums are strictly positive by (2), recovers \(w_{z1}\), \(u_{z1}\), and \(a_{zi}\) by positive-mass ratios.  Since the nonzero determinants in (8) are observable, every alternative treated decomposition has invertible factors in (5), and the same reconstruction applies to it.  The treated decomposition is therefore unique up to one common type permutation.  In particular, every globally compatible representation satisfies
\[
 a_{10}=a_{20}=\frac3{10},
 \qquad a_{11}=a_{21}=\frac45.
 \tag{14}
\]

The control conditional law does not depend on \(\vartheta\).  Define
\[
 g_{ij}=P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_3=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,D=0),
 \qquad
 h_{ij}=P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_3=1,X_4=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,D=0).
\]
Every conditioning event has positive probability by (2).  Exact substitution in (4) gives
\[
 (g_{ij})=
 \begin{pmatrix}41/115&111/230\\[2pt]23/45&11/30\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 (h_{ij})=
 \begin{pmatrix}103/575&174/575\\[2pt]49/225&14/75\end{pmatrix},
 \tag{15}
\]
and
\[
 P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_4=1\mid X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=0,D=0)=\frac12
 \quad(i,j\in\mathcal A).
 \tag{16}
\]
In an arbitrary compatible control decomposition, let \(\lambda_i=P(Z=1\mid X_1=i,D=0)\), \(q_{zj}=\kappa_{z0,3,j}\), and \(v_{zk}=\kappa_{z0,4,k}\).  Equation (14) makes \(Z\) conditionally independent of \(X_2\) given \((X_1,D=0)\), whence
\[
 g_{ij}=\lambda_iq_{1j}+(1-\lambda_i)q_{2j}.
 \tag{17}
\]
The observable differences are
\[
 g_{00}-g_{10}=-\frac{32}{207},
 \qquad g_{01}-g_{11}=\frac8{69}.
 \tag{18}
\]
Thus (17) implies \(\lambda_0\ne\lambda_1\) and \(q_{1j}\ne q_{2j}\) for both \(j\).  Multiplying (16) by the positive conditional probability of \(X_3=0\) yields, for \(i=0,1\),
\[
 \lambda_i(1-q_{1j})(v_{10}-1/2)
 +(1-\lambda_i)(1-q_{2j})(v_{20}-1/2)=0.
 \tag{19}
\]
The determinant of this pair of equations is
\[
 (\lambda_0-\lambda_1)(1-q_{1j})(1-q_{2j})\ne0,
\]
where the last inequality uses (18) and the strict upper probability bound in (2).  Consequently
\[
 v_{10}=v_{20}=\frac12.
 \tag{20}
\]

For the noncollided terminal row, (15), (17), and (18) give
\[
 \beta_j=\frac{h_{0j}-h_{1j}}{g_{0j}-g_{1j}},
 \qquad (\beta_0,\beta_1)=\left(\frac14,1\right),
\]
and
\[
 h_{ij}-\beta_jg_{ij}=c_j,
 \qquad (c_0,c_1)=\left(\frac9{100},-\frac9{50}\right).
 \tag{21}
\]
Because \(\lambda_0\ne\lambda_1\), equality of the two affine mixtures in (21) implies the component equalities
\[
 q_{z0}(v_{z1}-1/4)=\frac9{100},
 \qquad q_{z1}(v_{z1}-1)=-\frac9{50}
 \quad(z=1,2).
 \tag{22}
\]
Similarly, the two identities \(g_{i1}=3(1-g_{i0})/4\), evaluated at the two distinct values \(\lambda_0,\lambda_1\) in (17), imply
\[
 q_{z1}=\frac34(1-q_{z0})
 \quad(z=1,2).
 \tag{23}
\]
Writing \(x=q_{z0}\) and \(v=v_{z1}\), equations (22)--(23) reduce to
\[
 x(v-1/4)=\frac9{100},
 \qquad (1-x)(1-v)=\frac6{25}.
\]
Elimination of \(x\) gives the square-free equation
\[
 50v^2-55v+14=(5v-2)(10v-7)=0.
 \tag{24}
\]
Its discriminant is \(225>0\).  Equation (18) rules out assigning the same root to both types, so the unordered control triples are exactly
\[
 (q_{z0},q_{z1},v_{z1})
 \in\left\{
 \left(\frac35,\frac3{10},\frac25\right),
 \left(\frac15,\frac35,\frac7{10}\right)
 \right\}.
 \tag{25}
\]
For the second triple in (25), (15) and (17) give \((\lambda_0,\lambda_1)=(14/23,2/9)\).  Since \(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}(X_1=0\mid D=0)=23/50\), its control weight and initial-state probability are
\[
 w_{10}=\frac{23}{50}\frac{14}{23}+\frac{27}{50}\frac29=\frac25,
 \qquad
 u_{10}=\frac{(27/50)(2/9)}{2/5}=\frac3{10}.
 \tag{26}
\]
The other component consequently has weight \(3/5\) and initial-state probability \(7/10\).  This recovers the displayed control decomposition up to permutation.  Under the labeling of (26), the two determinants in (19) are
\[
 \frac{128}{1035}\quad\text{and}\quad\frac{112}{1035}.
 \tag{27}
\]
Equations (8), (11), (18), (24), and (27) show explicitly that every recovery minor and discriminant used here stays nonzero uniformly along the family.

The treated and control decompositions are separately unique up to permutation.  Hence there are precisely two relative alignments.  The identities following from the posterior-weight definition are
\[
 \pi_z=p_0w_{z0}+p_1w_{z1},
 \qquad e_z=\frac{p_1w_{z1}}{\pi_z}.
 \tag{28}
\]
Pairing control weights \((2/5,3/5)\) with treated weights \((3/5,2/5)\) in the displayed order gives \((\pi_1,\pi_2)=(1/2,1/2)\) and \((e_1,e_2)=(3/5,2/5)\).  Crossing the pairing gives \((\pi_1,\pi_2)=(3/5,2/5)\) and \((e_1,e_2)=(1/2,1/2)\).  Both have strict box slack, and (28) permits no third alignment.

For either relative alignment and either simultaneous labeling, the first terminal difference defining \(\Theta_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\) is zero, while the absolute values of the other three differences are
\[
 \left(\left|\frac7{10}-\frac25\right|,
 \left|\frac15-\frac45\right|,
 \left|\frac7{10}-\frac3{10}\right|\right)
 =\left(\frac3{10},\frac35,\frac25\right).
 \tag{29}
\]
Thus every compatible representation belongs to \(\Theta_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\).  Equations (2)--(29) prove \(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\), the asserted labeled-fiber equality, and the equality of the global and one-collision quotient fibers with exactly two classes.

By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}quotient\text{-}att}\), simultaneous type permutations do not alter \(\tau\).  It remains to evaluate one representative of each quotient class.  For the displayed alignment, the untreated recursions give
\[
 (m_{12},m_{13},m_{14})=\left(\frac12,\frac25,\frac{29}{50}\right),
 \qquad
 (m_{22},m_{23},m_{24})=\left(\frac35,\frac{21}{50},\frac{229}{500}\right).
 \tag{30}
\]
Only the type-one treated transition from \(X_2=0\) varies.  By (3) and \(P(X_2=0\mid Z=1,D=1)=1-m_{12}=1/2\),
\[
 O_3(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})

 =\frac{111}{250}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10}.
 \tag{31}

The type-one treated date-four transition difference is \(c_{141}-c_{140}=1/2\), so
\[
 O_4(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
 =\frac{259}{500}+w_{11}(1-m_{12})(c_{141}-c_{140})\vartheta
 =\frac{259}{500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}.
 \tag{32}

For the crossed alignment, the corresponding untreated recursions are
\[
 (m_{12},m_{13},m_{14})=\left(\frac12,\frac9{20},\frac{91}{200}\right),
 \qquad
 (m_{22},m_{23},m_{24})=\left(\frac35,\frac{11}{25},\frac{147}{250}\right).
 \tag{33}
\]
Weighting (30) and (33) by the treated posterior weights \((3/5,2/5)\) gives, respectively,
\[
 \left(\sum_z w_{z1}m_{z3},\sum_z w_{z1}m_{z4}\right)
 =\left(\frac{51}{125},\frac{332}{625}\right)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \left(\frac{223}{500},\frac{2541}{5000}\right).
 \tag{34}
\]
Subtracting (34) from (31)--(32) proves
\[
 \tau(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta};P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
 =\left(\frac9{250}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10},
 -\frac{33}{2500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}\right),
 \tag{35}
\]
\[
 \tau(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta};P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
 =\left(-\frac1{500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10},
 \frac{49}{5000}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}\right).
 \tag{36}
\]
Fiber exhaustion makes these the exact sharp joint image, rather than merely an outer bound.  The coordinate gaps are \(19/500\) and \(23/1000\), independently of \(\vartheta\), proving the stated marginal images and their specialization at \(\vartheta=0\).

Finally,
\[
 P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta,00111}-P^{\diamond}_{0,00111}
 =\left(\frac12\frac35\frac35\frac7{10}\frac7{10}\right)\vartheta
 =\frac{441}{5000}\vartheta.
 \tag{37}
\]
Thus \(\vartheta\mapsto P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\) is affine and injective.  Its image is a nondegenerate one-dimensional open affine segment inside the one-collision model.  Rational \(\vartheta\)'s give rational primitives and rational full-path cells and are dense in the parameter interval.  This proves positive-dimensional rational persistence without asserting relative openness in a larger collision variety.

We close by verifying the directed exact execution at \(\eta=1/10\) and \(\vartheta=0\).  This is a check of the preceding mathematics, not an additional general theorem.  With the cell key ordered as \(ijkld\), direct evaluation of \(F\) gives the following complete full-path table; the last two columns are \(P^{\diamond}_{ijkl0}\) and \(P^{\diamond}_{ijkl1}\):
\[
\begin{array}{c c c c|c c}

Exact summation of (38) yields \(\sum_{ijkld}P^{\diamond}_{ijkld}=1\) and \(p_0=p_1=1/2\).  Substitution of both \(\psi^{\diamond}\) and \(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\), and of their simultaneous swaps, gives zero in all thirty-two cellwise residuals against (38).

Order the orientation signs as \(s=(s_{0,1-k_0},s_{1,0},s_{1,1})\).  The complete accepted-label calculation uses
\[
\begin{aligned}
y_{AA}&=(1/5,4/5,7/10,3/10,7/10,2/5,98/625,21/625,12/625,24/625),\\
y_{AB}&=(1/5,4/5,7/10,3/10,2/5,7/10,63/1250,189/5000,21/625,147/625),\\

\end{aligned}
 \tag{39}
\]
For each of the signs \((+,-,+),(-,-,+),(+,+,-),(-,+,-)\), both \(\sigma=\mathrm{id}\) and \(\sigma=\mathrm{sw}\) are accepted, using \(y_{AA},y_{AB},y_{BA},y_{BB}\), respectively.  For each of these eight labels, exact substitution makes the eight \(\rho\)-equalities and four \(\gamma\)-equalities zero; makes all three orientation atoms strictly positive; and makes all thirty-two \(R_{zd}(i,j,k)-\eta^5\) atoms and all fifty-four cleared primitive-box atoms nonnegative.  Thus all \(101\) displayed branch atoms are checked.  Separately, the three required collision minors are zero and the reconstructed common collided probability is \(1/2\in[1/10,9/10]\).  Reconstruction returns, as appropriate, one member of
\[
 \{\psi^{\diamond},\ \mathrm{sw}\,\psi^{\diamond},\
 \psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}},\ \mathrm{sw}\,\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}\},
\]
and a further thirty-two-cell substitution verifies \(F(\psi)=P^{\diamond}\) for every accepted label.

The remaining twenty-four labels are also exhausted exactly.  Every one of the sixteen labels with \(k_0=1\) requires the observable collision equality
\[
 \chi_{01}^{01}
 =N_0(0,1,1)H_0(0,0,1)-N_0(0,0,1)H_0(0,1,1)=0,
\]
but direct evaluation from (38) gives

 \chi_{01}^{01}=\frac{11907}{12500000}>0.
 \tag{40}
\]
For each of the other eight labels, \(k_0=0\) and the two treated signs agree.  Before orientation signs are imposed, the treated part of the complete equality-and-box lifting is exhausted by
\[
 (5v_{110}-1)(5v_{110}-4)=0.
 \tag{41}
\]
The root \(v_{110}=1/5\), with isolator \((3/20,1/4)\), back-substitutes to \((v_{210},v_{111},v_{211})=(4/5,7/10,3/10)\); the root \(v_{110}=4/5\), with isolator \((3/4,17/20)\), back-substitutes to \((1/5,3/10,7/10)\).  The control recovery equation (24) has the two roots \(2/5\) and \(7/10\), which give the two labeled control solutions in (39).  Hence their cross-product is exactly the four rational algebraic equality leaves \(y_{AA},y_{AB},y_{BA},y_{BB}\) for each alignment.  At any leaf whose actual control orientation disagrees with the branch label, the first violated atom is \(s_{01}(v_{101}-v_{201})>0\), with exact value \(-3/10\).  Of the remaining two leaves, if both required treated signs are positive, the treated-\(A\) leaf violates \(v_{110}-v_{210}>0\) with value \(-3/5\), while the treated-\(B\) leaf violates \(v_{111}-v_{211}>0\) with value \(-2/5\). It follows from the eight accepted witnesses and the twenty-four exhaustive rejection certificates that the exact normalized output is
\[
 \bigl[(250q_3-9=0)\wedge(2500q_4+33=0)\bigr]
 \vee
 \bigl[(500q_3+1=0)\wedge(5000q_4-49=0)\bigr].
 \tag{42}
\]
The marginals are \((500q_3+1=0)\vee(250q_3-9=0)\) and \((2500q_4+33=0)\vee(5000q_4-49=0)\).  The four primitive linear endpoint polynomials have, respectively, the rational isolating intervals
\[
 (-1/400,-1/600),\quad(1/30,1/25),\quad
 (-7/500,-13/1000),\quad(9/1000,1/100),
\]
and each has Thom sign sequence \((0,+)\), because its derivative is the positive leading integer coefficient.

The machine-readable artifact \(\operatorname{art{:}p\text{-}diamond\text{-}onecollisionatt\text{-}v1}\) stores (38), every exact \(H\), \(N\), and \(\chi\) value, all \(101\) canonical branch-atom evaluations for every accepted label, the complete four-leaf records just described for every same-treated-sign rejection and the collision-minor record for every wrong-state rejection, all reconstructed structural vectors, the cellwise residuals, the ATT values, and (42).  Its deterministic reduced-fraction replay recomputes rather than assumes these values and compares the complete canonical serialization byte for byte.  This establishes the requested bounded execution instance and makes no certificate-compression, global-atlas, near-collision, asymptotic, or tier claim.

proposed.statement:
For every rational \(0<\eta<3/20\) and every real \(\vartheta\) with \(|\vartheta|<1/100\), one has \(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta},\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\in\Theta_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\) and
\[
F(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})=F(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta})=P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}.
\]
The labeled global fiber is
\[
\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta})
=\{\sigma\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}:\sigma\in\mathfrak S_2\}
\cup\{\sigma\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}:\sigma\in\mathfrak S_2\}.
\]
Consequently the global and one-collision quotient fibers coincide and have exactly the two classes represented by \(\psi^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\) and \(\psi^{\diamond,\mathrm{sw}}_{\vartheta}\). Their ATT vectors are, respectively,
\[
\left(\frac{9}{250}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10},-\frac{33}{2500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}\right)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\left(-\frac{1}{500}+\frac{3\vartheta}{10},\frac{49}{5000}+\frac{3\vartheta}{20}\right).
\]
Thus each marginal sharp image consists of the corresponding two displayed coordinates, with gaps \(19/500\) and \(23/1000\). The map \(\vartheta\mapsto P^{\diamond}_{\vartheta}\) is affine and injective. Its image is therefore a positive-dimensional persistence family inside the one-collision model, and it contains a dense rational subfamily. At \(\vartheta=0\) this gives \(\mathcal I_{0,3}^{1\mathrm c}(P^{\diamond})=\{-1/500,9/250\}\) and \(\mathcal I_{0,4}^{1\mathrm c}(P^{\diamond})=\{-33/2500,49/5000\}\). No relative-openness claim in a larger collision variety is made.
proposed.justification: An explicit injective one-parameter family proves that the disconnected two-value geometry persists on a positive-dimensional subset rather than occurring at one isolated observed law; the exact rational execution artifact audits its zero-perturbation member.
proposed.gap: Generic label switching does not establish a causal ATT gap after quotienting simultaneous labels, and the cited mixture papers provide no exact one-collision persistence family with two aggregate-ATT values.
proposed.consumer: Regression tests for the public package can replay the rational benchmark, verify both branch witnesses and their fixed ATT gaps, and prevent replacement of the attained two-point set by its interval hull.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This dependency synchronization connects the proposition's independently recomputed zero-perturbation audit to the exact branch algorithm and the mandated execution artifact; the proposition's formal claim is unchanged.
